title: Ring rule stays; a protocol exists only where two production adapters exist (retires P-01/P-08 'every adapter behind a port, only the container wires it')
context: P-01 (features-no-infrastructure) and P-08 (cli-no-infrastructure) required every I/O boundary to sit behind a core/protocols Protocol wired only by container.py. Measured reality (0.5.1 deepening audit, re-verified by inspection): core/protocols holds 23 Protocol classes in 22 files, 935 LOC of interface text; only 4 have two or more production adapters — TelemetryRefreshLock, FilePermissionSetter, ShutdownHandler (posix/windows pairs) and ProcessAncestry (Linux proc / ps / Windows toolhelp) — all OS-portability seams; the other 19 have exactly one infrastructure implementer and exist only to satisfy the two contracts. container.py is 880 LOC, 22 fix commits, 10 ledger records carrying 'container.py' as component, ~180 LOC of dead lifecycle closures (_definition_committer, _closure_committer, _memory_lint_gate, _repo_hygiene_sweeper, _workspace_python_bin, resolve_context) kept alive by the funnel. Ledger evidence: a grep of every 'cause'/'solution' field in specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl finds ONE mention of 'adapter' (git shallow-repo guard, fixed inside GitSubprocessClient — not a swap) and ZERO mentions of 'fake'; no bug was ever fixed by substituting an adapter behind a seam. The contracts produced the funnel they were meant to prevent: every verb needing infrastructure added a build_* function to container.py instead of a port, and 9 of the 18 capped ignore edges are exceptions to these two contracts alone (features-no-infrastructure 7, cli-no-infrastructure 2). Test fakes are not a second adapter: git_subprocess has 14 real-adapter test files and 0 fakes.
decision: We will keep the ring rule — core imports nothing internal; infrastructure imports only core; features import core and infrastructure; cli and hooks import all of them; no upward edge; features never import a sibling feature; core.kernel_tunables stays a leaf; core.specs_resolver keeps its single home — and drop the port requirement: a feature or a CLI verb imports the concrete infrastructure class it is the only consumer of, directly. A Protocol lives in core/protocols only where two or more PRODUCTION adapters exist (today: TelemetryRefreshLock, FilePermissionSetter, ShutdownHandler, ProcessAncestry); a test fake never counts as a second adapter. container.py wires only what two features share or what a platform seam selects; everything else is constructed where it is consumed. Replacement Part-1 text — P-01: 'We keep the dependency ring: core imports nothing internal, infrastructure imports only core, no layer imports upward; a feature imports the concrete infrastructure class it alone consumes.' Measured by: `lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache` — contracts core-no-upper-layers and infrastructure-no-upper-layers (zero ignored imports). P-08: 'We keep a Protocol in core/protocols only where two production adapters exist; container.py composes platform seams and shared collaborators, nothing single-consumer.' Measured by: `pytest tests/contract/test_protocols_have_two_adapters.py` (AST walk: every class under core/protocols has >= 2 implementers under infrastructure/), landing in the same commit that retires the 19 single-adapter protocols.
consequences: + setup.cfg: contracts features-no-infrastructure and cli-no-infrastructure are DELETED with their 9 ignore edges; _RECORDED_IGNORE_EDGE_CAP drops 18 -> 9 and _RECORDED_CONTRACT_COUNT 9 -> 7 in the accept commit (P-10 ratchet holds: the cap only falls). The cross-feature edges (6) stay until K7; the features-no-subprocess edges (3) stay under P-02, which is untouched (one process seam, not a swap seam). + ~17 protocol files, their build_* indirections and the two-protocols-per-store pairs are deleted (~935 -> ~200 LOC of protocol text); container.py shrinks to wiring only (~250 LOC); the ~180 LOC dead closures go with it. + Tests use real adapters over tmp dirs, as git_subprocess already does; mirrored fake-based unit files are deleted per dd-test-stewardship. - A feature reaching an adapter directly cannot be substituted without editing the feature; accepted because the ledger shows zero substitutions in the project's history and four real seams remain protected. - P-01/P-08 text in ARCHITECTURE.md changes in the accept commit (`docs(adr): accept ...`), never before. Bug surface: REDUCED — the 880-LOC funnel with 22 fix commits and 10 ledger records is the only component this decision touches, and it shrinks; no ledger bug depends on the retired seams. Dependency: K9's deletion half (dead closures, single-consumer modules filed inside their feature where no contract breaks) proceeds before acceptance; protocol retirement and contract deletion wait for the operator's accept.
measured_by: lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache — contracts core-no-upper-layers, infrastructure-no-upper-layers, features-no-cross-feature, kernel-tunables-is-a-leaf, bind-resolution-seam-is-a-single-home; plus pytest tests/contract/test_import_linter_ignore_cap.py re-pinned at _RECORDED_IGNORE_EDGE_CAP = 9, _RECORDED_CONTRACT_COUNT = 7

title: Git index boundary: one session per checkout is operator practice, not library code; the two shared-index bugs are deferred with that reason
context: Two open records — concurrent-sessions-share-git-index-commit-boundary-contamination (2026-08-27, `git commit --amend` swept a peer's staged histo file) and concurrent-agent-git-add-clobbers-other-sessions-staged-files-into-unrelated-commit (2026-08-27, `git add -A` swept a peer's two staged files) — have one cause: two harness sessions ran Bash in the SAME checked-out repos/<slug> tree, and git keeps exactly one index per worktree. Three options were weighed. (a) `context bind` provisions a per-session linked worktree: bind writes one session record and acquires nothing (context-management memory); a harness process cannot change its cwd after launch, so a worktree created by bind is never the tree the session commits from; gitflow allows exactly one live feature/{M.m.p} and git refuses the same branch checked out in two worktrees, so every extra worktree needs its own branch or a detached HEAD — a second branch pattern the §4 contract forbids; the open bug sdd-gate-memory-phase-resolves-empty-when-cwd-is-a-linked-worktree-outside-repos shows worktrees already break resolution (K1 fixes it); Windows adds per-worktree venv cost. Rejected. (b) pre-commit refuses when the index holds paths staged by a foreign presence: PresenceRecord carries session_id, runtime, pid, last_seen_at — no paths — so the gate would have to start recording every written path per session (new state, new reaper), git cannot attribute who ran `git add`, and the refusal blocks a human commit, violating DADAIA §3.4 (pre-commit warns and always allows) and the NO-LOCKS doctrine. A branch added to pre_commit_decision plus a new record kind is the puxadinho the standing order forbids. Rejected. (c) Nothing in the library: the index is a per-worktree resource by git's own contract; DADAIA §7.3 already states 'commit exactly what the fix touched, never a blanket -A'; the only missing statement is the operator practice.
decision: We will not add library code for the git index. The practice is: one harness session per checked-out tree; an operator who wants parallel sessions on one repo creates the linked worktree BEFORE launching the harness (`git worktree add ../<repo_slug>-<n> <branch>`) and launches it there, so each session owns its own index; every agent stages by explicit path and commits with `git commit --only <paths>` or after a path-scoped `git add`, never `-A` and never a bare `--amend` (DADAIA §7.3 already). The two records move to terminal `deferred` with reason: 'shared git index between two sessions in one checkout is a git contract, not a library contract; practice = one session per checkout/worktree; revisit only if a harness gains a per-session cwd'. Code change: 0 production LOC; owner: none — the practice belongs to the operator and to the law text (a one-line statement under DADAIA.md §3.3 'Races, mode, context', authored by ai-engineer in public/data/DADAIA.md if the operator wants it written).
consequences: + Zero new state, zero new branch, zero new reaper; pre_commit_decision stays WARN-only; presence stays path-less and advisory; bind keeps acquiring nothing; Invocation keeps one session_id. + The K1 fix for the linked-worktree resolution bug makes the practice actually work end to end (a worktree outside repos/ resolves its context). - The defect can still recur whenever an operator launches two harnesses in one tree; the pre-commit advisory WARN ('another session is live on this context') is the only signal, and it already exists. Bug surface: UNCHANGED for the library (no touched feature), and the two records leave the open set with a reason instead of a patch — the 06-10..07-22 session-model chain shows every structural fix in this area was a deletion, never an added guard.
measured_by: dadaia bugs status — both records terminal `deferred` naming this decision; pytest tests/contract/test_hooks_publication_boundary.py (pre-commit remains allow-always)

title: One Invocation: session, context, workspace, mode, release and phase are resolved once per process in core.invocation (amends P-09's single home)
context: P-09 named core.specs_resolver.resolve_context as the single home, yet eight modules re-derived context, three re-derived the session id and four re-derived staleness from the same files; 28+ ledger records, one open (sdd-gate-memory-phase-resolves-empty-when-cwd-is-a-linked-worktree-outside-repos). A single home for one fact was not enough while the neighbouring facts had many. P-09 carries `ADR: none` (pre-canon principle); this record is its first decision.
decision: We resolve the whole Invocation (workspace_root, session_id, context_name, repo_slug, specs_dir, mode, release, phase, rung) once per process in core.invocation.resolve and pass the value to every policy; the session record has exactly one owner in core; no module outside core.invocation reads .dadaia/sessions/ or derives a context.
consequences: + P-09 text changes its named home to core.invocation.resolve; the import-linter contract bind-resolution-seam-is-a-single-home names core.invocation and keeps zero ignore edges. + hooks build the Invocation from the payload; CLI from flags; container no longer resolves. - core.specs_resolver, core.session_env, features/spec_context/session_identity and the eight ladders are deleted. Risk: any caller that still re-derives a fact is a regression; measured by the contract test.
measured_by: lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache — contract bind-resolution-seam-is-a-single-home (core.invocation, zero ignored imports); pytest tests/unit/core/test_invocation.py; grep -rn 'sessions/' dadaia_workspace --include=*.py | grep -v core/invocation returns nothing

title: P-14/P-15 name release-state-v1: RELEASE.json is one mutable state document; core.release_state stays I/O-free and its envelope closed (amends the pre-canon P-14/P-15 measured-by, whose artifacts were deleted at 0.5.0 S1)
context: P-14 and P-15 (ADR: none, pre-canon) measure `core/release_events.py` read-only-ness and the seven-kind RELEASE.jsonl event envelope via tests/contract/test_release_events_read_only.py and test_release_event_schema.py. All three artifacts were deleted when the operator ruled RELEASE.jsonl -> RELEASE.json (commit 32a64e88, 'a highly mutable state file, not append-only'). The successors exist: core/release_state.py (parse/serialize only, zero file I/O), public/schemas/releases/release-state-v1.schema.json (additionalProperties: false at every level, log entries closed on ts/agent/kind/text), tests/contract/test_release_state_read_only.py and test_release_state_schema.py. The principles' substance is unchanged; only their named artifacts are stale, which MEM-DRIFT flags on every doctor run. Accepted by operator decision 2026-09-12 (release 0.4.7 candidate 1, FR8).
decision: We keep both principles and re-point them: P-14 'We keep the release-state reader pure: core/release_state.py parses and serializes already-read text and performs no file I/O' measured by pytest tests/contract/test_release_state_read_only.py; P-15 'We close the release-state envelope: release-state-v1 carries additionalProperties: false at every level, a closed log-entry shape, and no harness session_id' measured by pytest tests/contract/test_release_state_schema.py. No code change.
consequences: + Two stale Part-1 pointers become live checks; MEM-DRIFT no longer names deleted files. + Zero LOC. - None. Bug surface: UNCHANGED (documentation fidelity only). The Part-1 hunk lands with this proposal because it is a rename of measured-by artifacts, not a change of principle; the operator's accept flips status only.

title: Release-candidates system: one live open-scope release named last-published-PyPI + 1 patch, growing by closed-scope candidates
decision: Release-candidates system: one live open-scope release named last-published-PyPI+1-patch; candidates are closed-scope SDD cycles; version increments and next branch is cut ONLY on operator-approved deploy — reason: Since 0.4.4 four internal version ids and multiple branches accumulated without a publication — version/branch slop the operator ordered eliminated; the PyPI lineage is the only axis (extends v0.4.2 R2)
consequences: specs/releases/<v>/ holds the live trio at root; completed scopes archive to rc-N/ subfolders; exactly one live release and one live feature branch
measured_by: SPEC-DOC-045 — pyproject [tool.poetry].version equals the live release id once the release reaches CLOSURE/ARCHIVED, so a version moves only at the operator-approved deploy

decision: Retire the scaffolded segment lane (alpha-N/rc-N sub-phase dirs with **Segment:** headers) entirely; rc-N under a release means only an archived candidate trio — reason: Two semantics for one folder name breed drift; the operator chose one mechanism

decision: Rename RELEASE.json to _RELEASE.json everywhere, including specs/releases/_archive/* — reason: Underscore prefix groups the state file with _archive/_ideas and sorts it apart from the working trio — folder legibility

title: Candidate gate mechanics: new CLI verb `dadaia release rc-archive` executes the continue ruling (trio to rc-N/, phase reset)
decision: Candidate gate mechanics: new CLI verb `dadaia release rc-archive` executes the deterministic archival; the promote-or-continue question after each feature->develop merge is agent protocol, never a hook — reason: Hooks never block humans (DADAIA §3.5); mechanics deserve one deterministic executor
consequences: rc-archive validates candidate closure, moves the trio to rc-N, bumps the counter in _RELEASE.json

title: At approved deploy the final trio stays at the release root and the whole release folder is archived under _archive/<id>/
decision: At approved deploy the final trio stays at the release root and the whole release folder archives to _archive/<version>/ — reason: Root = what shipped, rc-N = the path there; immediate legibility
consequences: no rc folder is minted for the shipping scope

title: Slop is defined once by the deletion test, distributed over two classes and measured by downward-only ratchets
context: 'slop' was law on 14 surfaces and defined on none, with four implicit meanings and the same rule in up to five homes; no rule covered comments, docstrings, acronyms or SPEC size; constitution §12 (since v0.1.46) did not hold while ratchets V26-V30 did (report 2026-09-03T023255Z-slop-governance-map; operator ruling 2026-09-03 on two distribution classes): rewritten 2026-09-12 (audit ADR-2: named P-29 and an amended P-24 that never existed); accepted by operator decision 2026-09-12
decision: We define slop ONCE, by the deletion test, in DADAIA.md §7.6, and distribute it over two classes: the agentic-class statements stay in §7.6, and the artifact-class statements live as fixed sections projected by the scaffold into constitution.md (slop-law), memory/ARCHITECTURE.md (slop-code) and memory/QUALITY.md (slop-tests), kept byte-exact by the doctor's FIXED-1/FIXED-2 rules; constitution §12 points at §7.6 instead of restating it. The balance is measured by downward-only ratchets: V31 (test files without an `Intent:` header, per tier) in tests/contract/test_test_suite_ratchets.py, and V32 (governance ids in production comments and docstrings), V33 (PREFIX-NN families without a mechanical reader) and V34 (live candidate SPEC.md/TASKS.md bytes) in tests/contract/test_slop_ratchets.py. Detection signals live in dd-code-review/SLOP.md, read by review and by audit pillar 2.
consequences:
+ one definition, one home per statement: a reader greps `deletion test` and finds §7.6, and every artifact restatement is a healed projection rather than a hand-kept copy
+ the balance is a number that only moves down, so 'we cleaned slop' is falsifiable
- four ratchet ceilings must be lowered by hand at each closure, or they rot upward-permissive

title: P-16 deleted: no derived provenance is stored, so nothing needs to equal a re-derivation
context: operator grill ruling 2026-09-12 (SDD lifecycle audit; release 0.4.7 candidate 3 SPEC FR1) — the operator directive of 2026-09-12 (implement and close every registered item) makes the ruling's records accepted at append. P-16 ('a stored resolved_commit equals the value derived from git history') measured a seven-key git-derived cache on the bug record (lineage_source, registration_commit, registration_granularity, resolved_commit, resolution_granularity, root_cause, migration_note) written by core/bug_provenance.py from a full-history walk every CI job fetched (fetch-depth: 0 x13); its only reader was audit pillar 1, which reads git log for the same fact and wrote the cache back; 476 live and 65 archived records carried keys nothing consumed.
decision: Delete P-16 together with the field it measured. The bug record stores no fact a resolver can re-derive from git: core/bug_provenance.py, core/models/git_history.py, GitSubprocessClient.log_added_lines, BugEventKind, BugService.resolved_commit and the seven schema keys are deleted; BugRecord.from_dict ignores exactly the seven retired keys and to_dict never emits them; dadaia doctor --fix (LEDGER-BUGS-SCHEMA) re-serializes every committed record that still carries one; CI checks out at default depth except security-verdict-gate. Lineage stays a declared fact — caused_by, written once at bugs resolve and validated against the ledger or the literal none — because it is a judgement, not a derivation.
consequences:
+ one record shape, one lineage writer, no cache to keep honest and no principle guarding it
+ every CI job but one is a shallow checkout
+ git is the only authority for git facts; pillar 1 reads git log directly
- a consumer tree with pre-0.4.7 records is invalid until dadaia doctor --fix runs once (the fix line is printed under every finding)
- the retired-key tuple in from_dict is a migration and is deletable once every consumer tree has run the fix

title: Every human- and agent-facing document derives from a named memory atom under a content hash
context: operator demand 2026-09-12: the tool must be usable by humans and by agents, and the docs are bad and stale. README.md (15 KB, hand-written beside memory, PyPI's long description) carried eleven verified dead claims (ACTIVE.md/CLOSURE.md, four harnesses, a TTL lease with a PID veto, six-axis reviews, handoffs under specs/releases, event-sourced bugs, dadaia academy and dadaia clean, Academy/Games tabs, memory writable only in two phases, a pre-commit lease gate) and a hand-kept CLI table with two dead verbs; nothing measured a README sentence against the atom that should have produced it, and two of three discovery surfaces (PyPI metadata, the GitHub repository) said nothing. Release 0.4.7 candidate 4 (SPEC FR3/FR4/FR5, Q8) admits the rule as QUALITY.md P-29 with this record proposed; the operator flips it.
decision: We derive every human- and agent-facing document from a named memory atom under a content hash: README.md, llms.txt and every docs/*.md carry under each `## ` heading one or more `<!-- derived-from: <slug> sha256:<12 hex> -->` markers whose slug resolves by stem to exactly one file under specs/memory/ and whose hash is that file's current sha256 prefix; docs/cli.md carries no marker and is the committed output of `dadaia help tree`; there is no generator verb — a stale section is re-derived by a reader and its hash re-recorded in the same commit as the atom (dd-release-implementation MEMORY-UPDATE); the tagline is one sentence across README.md, pyproject.toml `description` and llms.txt; a section that can name no atom is slop, or names a fact memory lacks and the fact enters memory first.
consequences:
+ a doc cannot rot silently: one changed atom byte reddens every section derived from it, and the failure names the atom to re-read and the line to re-record
+ no fact enters a doc that memory does not carry, so memory stays the one product truth and the docs are its projections
+ one finder (features/specs/citations.py::dead_citations) keeps docs, public assets and memory free of dead verbs and paths
- the hash is whole-file: an atom edit touching no derived fact still costs a re-read of every section citing it
- the derived set is a glob: a new docs/*.md is governed at birth and cannot opt out
